api.access: Public HTTPS, token-gated by X-Internal-Token; only the Vercel server reads the origin and token

maps.provider: Leaflet with keyless OSM.de street tiles and Esri World Imagery satellite tiles

web.INTERNAL_API_BASE_URL: Koyeb HTTPS origin (https://wayfarer-api-....koyeb.app); server-only, do not use NEXT_PUBLIC_
web.INTERNAL_API_TOKEN: 32+ random chars, same value as the API secret

api.DATABASE_URL: Neon pooled connection string with sslmode=require
api.SMTP_PASSWORD: Gmail app password (never commit; use a Koyeb secret)

steps: Create a Neon project and copy the pooled DATABASE_URL into Koyeb secrets.
Run the migration job /app/migrate against Neon before the first deploy.
Build and deploy apps/api/Dockerfile to Koyeb with the koyeb.json values. Enable its HTTPS endpoint; /v1 rejects requests without the shared X-Internal-Token.
Set the Vercel project Root Directory to apps/web. Add INTERNAL_API_BASE_URL and INTERNAL_API_TOKEN in Vercel Project Settings (not in vercel.json).
Point WEB_ORIGIN and PUBLIC_WEB_URL at the final Vercel domain.
Set OTP_HMAC_SECRET, SESSION_SECRET, INTERNAL_API_TOKEN and SMTP_PASSWORD as Koyeb secrets; each required secret must be at least 32 characters.
Invite flow links use PUBLIC_WEB_URL; verify a full invitation round trip in production.
Maps use OSM.de and Esri World Imagery without an API key. If a tile provider is unavailable, the itinerary remains usable and the map shows a non-blocking notice.
